audit_findings.title: Post-anchor borrowing is missing from the levered earnings numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,500.0 million principal; approximately $6.0 million annual pretax effective interest at the filed 0.4% effective rate
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring issuance-cost amortization and financing expense reduce levered owner earnings; the borrowing proceeds are already included in bridge cash.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, our gross long-term debt totaled $3,004.9 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The period mismatch is demonstrated, but the new notes bear no regular interest. A $6.0 million annual reduction is 6.1% of the $98.1 million anchor and, mechanically using the base operating-PV multiple, reduces equity value by about $84 million or $0.16 per diluted share. That would not alter the conclusion relative to the $74.38 market price.
audit_findings.action: Recalculate forward owner earnings using the 2031 notes' filed effective-interest schedule and verify that hedge and issuance cash flows are not counted again in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year anchor may perpetuate an exceptional restructuring trough
audit_findings.magnitude: $980.5 million of filed FY2025 realignment-related charges: $666.9 million restructuring, impairment and other, $268.2 million inventory charges, and $45.4 million consumables, supplies and purchase-commitment charges
audit_findings.mechanism: Nonrecurring charges left in the $98.1 million owner-earnings anchor suppress every forecast year and terminal value; recurring restructuring, underutilization and economic inventory losses should remain expenses.
audit_findings.evidence: Our operating results were significantly impacted by restructuring, asset impairment and other charges resulting from our 2025 Manufacturing Realignment Program.
audit_findings.explanation: The exceptional-charge burden is approximately ten times the anchor and therefore can dominate the valuation. The error is not that all $980.5 million must be added back: repeated programs in 2023-2026 demonstrate that some restructuring behavior and capacity costs may be structural. The unresolved classification is nevertheless reasonably capable of changing the valuation substantially.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the anchor line by line, including tax effects, and rerun separate cases retaining recurring underutilization, recurring restructuring and genuine inventory destruction while excluding only demonstrated nonrecurring impairments and completed exit costs.

audit_findings.title: Vcore contingent cash consideration is an unbridged senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $113.1 million latest filed fair value; $144.0 million contractual maximum
audit_findings.mechanism: The cash-settled acquisition liability should reduce the equity bridge unless its expected cash cost has already reduced owner earnings or bridge cash.
audit_findings.evidence: The fair value of the contingent consideration was $ 109.9 million as of December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is demonstrated. Deducting the July 2026 fair value would reduce the $5,243 million base equity value by 2.2%, or about $0.21 per diluted share; even deducting the $144 million maximum changes value by only about $0.27 per share. Neither scale changes the valuation conclusion relative to the $74.38 market price.
audit_findings.action: Deduct the latest $113.1 million liability in a bridge rerun, then verify against milestone payments and remeasurement entries that the obligation is reflected exactly once.

audit_findings.title: Working-capital timing may have been treated as recurring owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $493.0 million favorable net FY2025 operating-cash-flow contribution from filed changes in receivables, inventories, other assets, accounts payable and other liabilities; amount embedded in the $98.1 million anchor is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A temporary working-capital release included in owner earnings would inflate the anchor, forecast cash generation and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Our operating cash flows for the year ended December 31, 2025 decreased by $146.6 million, or 7.7%, compared to the year ended December 31, 2024 and was primarily attributable to a reduction in net income driven by lower end-market demand for our products partially offset by the timing of cash receipts and payments related to working capital balances.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a large favorable balance-sheet contribution to operating cash flow, equal to about five times the anchor, but the supplied record does not show which working-capital adjustment entered the owner-earnings calculation or how much was ordinary. Materiality therefore cannot be established without the anchor reconciliation.
audit_findings.action: Trace each FY2025 working-capital line into the owner-earnings worksheet and rerun using a sustainable working-capital requirement tied to each revenue scenario.

audit_findings.title: The diluted-share ceiling and earnings numerator may represent incompatible convertible-note states
audit_findings.magnitude: 533.111721 million valuation shares versus 389.311721 million filed shares outstanding, a 143.8 million or 36.9% excess; denominator-only base value is $9.83 versus $13.47 using actual shares
audit_findings.mechanism: Conversion assumptions jointly affect diluted shares, continuing interest and issuance-cost expense, cash settlement of principal, note-hedge offsets, warrant dilution and bridge cash.
audit_findings.evidence: The 0.50 % Notes and the 0 % Notes are repayable in cash up to the par value and in cash or shares of common stock for the excess over par value.
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation combines a maximum dilution ceiling with continuing debt expense, which is not one internally consistent claim state. The 36.9% denominator difference is large enough to materially affect per-share value. The net direction is mixed because eliminating excess dilution raises value, while consistent cash settlement of principal may consume bridge cash; conversion may also remove interest and activate hedge offsets.
audit_findings.action: Rerun outstanding, converted and warrant-exercised states with matched shares, interest, issuance-cost amortization, principal cash settlement and hedge effects; retain the 533.111721 million denominator only as a separately labeled stress ceiling.

audit_findings.title: Government-incentive clawbacks could reverse benefits already embedded in earnings and assets
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed exposure categories include $151.9 million reducing PP&E cost and $19.4 million reducing FY2025 operating expenses
audit_findings.mechanism: A probable recapture would create a senior cash liability or operating expense and could reverse depreciation and expense benefits embedded in owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: If conditions are not satisfied or the duration period for the agreement is infringed, the incentives are subject to reduction, termination, or recapture.
audit_findings.explanation: The incentives and contractual recapture conditions are filed, but no present breach, probable obligation or maximum recapture amount is supplied. This is therefore a forward-looking compliance risk rather than a demonstrated valuation error. The recorded benefit amounts identify scale but do not establish recoverable exposure.
audit_findings.action: Monitor compliance by program, especially where workforce or capacity reductions affect conditions, and rerun only when a filing identifies noncompliance, a probable liability or a quantified maximum exposure.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Historical residuals of $32.9 million to $72.5 million; FY2024 residual $61.0 million, equal to 4.9% of FY2024 owner earnings; FY2025 anchor effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual D&A proven to be an eligible non-economic charge would be added back to owner earnings, increasing forecast cash flows and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2017 $32.9m (6.8% of filed D&A); FY2018 $37.7m (7.4% of filed D&A); FY2019 $68.2m (11.5% of filed D&A); FY2020 $60.7m (9.7% of filed D&A); FY2021 $61.2m (10.3% of filed D&A); FY2022 $72.5m (13.1% of filed D&A); FY2023 $67.4m (11.1% of filed D&A); FY2024 $61.0m (9.5% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: Leaving unidentified D&A as an expense is conservative, but the record does not classify the residual or provide the FY2025 amount affecting the anchor. Historical amounts show that the issue could matter against the much smaller $98.1 million anchor, yet they cannot establish the current-year adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the FY2025 D&A composition and add back only components supported by filed evidence as eligible non-economic charges, then rerun the valuation.
